scores.claim_text: GE Aerospace's XA100 next-generation large-combat engine architecture is positioned as a forward growth driver, supported by U.S. DoD and foreign-government budgets for fleet upgrade and modernization.
supports: pentagon_jbook(XA100) = NOT_FOUND

pentagon_jbook(PE 0604010F Next Generation Adaptive Propulsion) = FUNDED_STEADY ($573.8M FY24)
pentagon_jbook(PE 0604004F Advanced Engine Development) = FUNDED_STEADY ($270.0M FY24)

M_value.XA100: NOT_FOUND (corpus does not catalog the XA100 demonstrator name directly)

scores.interpretation: Apply heuristic #3 (reorganization caveat) + #4 (PE name ambiguity): XA100 was the GE entrant in the Adaptive Engine Transition Program (AETP, originally PE 0604004F-funded). In FY24 budgeting, AF cancelled the F-35 re-engine path (no XA100 production decision) and FOLDED adaptive-cycle work into the new Next Generation Adaptive Propulsion (NGAP, PE 0604010F) — which IS funded, at $573.8M. So XA100 the *named product* has been effectively cancelled as an F-35 re-engine, but adaptive-cycle propulsion R&D continues at NGAP. The narrative claim 'support for next generation large-combat engine architecture such as Aerospace's XA100 program' overstates: XA100 itself is not a Pentagon line, and the AETP program-of-record path was terminated; NGAP is a re-compete that GE must win against P&W. MODERATE because the broader propulsion-R&D bucket survives and GE remains a credible bidder, but the specifically-named product (XA100) is no longer a J-Book line.

summary.thesis_summary: GE Aerospace's J-Book exposure at 2024-09-01 is structurally sound: B-21, F-15EX, F-35 sustainment, and NGAP are all FUNDED_STEADY in the FY26 books. Two soft signals warrant a MODERATE flag: (1) the specifically-named XA100 product is no longer a J-Book line — AETP terminated, NGAP is a re-compete GE must win; (2) Defense engine unit shipments dropped -12% YoY despite 'strong demand' narrative, suggesting platform-mix headwinds that the company has not localized for investors. T901/FARA (the most narratively-emphasized Army win) cannot be verified — J-Book corpus is AF/Space/DARPA-heavy and lacks Army PEs, a known coverage gap. The 6-7% defense mix is small relative to GE's $68B total revenue, so even a severe Pentagon shock would be margin-not-existential.
